name: Melatiah
overview: Melatiah was a male figure identified as a Gibeonite who contributed to the restoration efforts during the rebuilding of Jerusalem. He is noted specifically for making repairs to the official seat of the governor, reflecting his role in the community's physical and administrative restoration. Beyond this, Scripture provides limited personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Melatiah means 'YHWH sets free,' indicating a theophoric element that acknowledges God's deliverance. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 3:7, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a significant spiritual meaning consistent with biblical naming conventions.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Melatiah beyond what is noted in his unique attribute as a Gibeonite involved in repair work. There are no additional relationships listed or implied in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Melatiah's significance lies in his contribution to the rebuilding of Jerusalem's governance infrastructure after the exile. As a Gibeonite, his participation underscores the inclusion of diverse groups in the restoration process under God's providence. His work on the governor's official seat highlights the practical efforts necessary to reestablish order and leadership in the post-exilic community.
